extracted.intended_audience: registrants and preparers of SEC filings (management, CFOs, corporate accountants, legal counsel, and auditors)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing Management's Discussion & Analysis (MD&A) narrative for SEC filings consistent with S-K 303, Item 5 of Form 20-F, and related SEC interpretive guidance; covers liquidity, results of operations, KPIs, critical estimates, interim requirements, pro forma presentation, and related-party disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall MD&A objective [S-K 303(a)]
rubrics_metrics.description: MD&A is a narrative explanation of the financial statements and other statistical data that the registrant believes will enhance a readers’ understanding of its financial condition, cash flows and other changes in financial condition and results of operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should discuss and analyze, from management’s perspective: material information relevant to an assessment of financial condition and results of operations (including evaluation of amounts and certainty of cash flows); material events and uncertainties reasonably likely to cause reported information not to be indicative of future results or condition; and matters that have had a material impact on reported operations or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on future operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic or boilerplate disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: MD&A should not consist of generic or boilerplate disclosure; S-K 303 is principles-based to provide flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MD&A should reflect facts and circumstances specific to each registrant rather than canned language. The staff's release suggested presenting most material information early, using headers/bullets/tables to improve readability and omitting immaterial information (these suggestions are not themselves S-K 303 requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidity and capital resources — short- and long-term analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an analysis of the registrant's ability to generate and obtain adequate amounts of cash to meet requirements and plans for cash in the short-term (next 12 months) and separately in the long-term (beyond 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on ability to meet obligations and management's plans for liquidity over these distinct horizons; discuss material sources of cash and plans to address shortfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss known trends, demands, commitments affecting liquidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any known trends, demands, commitments, events or uncertainties reasonably likely to result in a material increase or decrease in liquidity should be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a material deficiency is identified, disclose the course of action taken or proposed to remedy it. Identify and separately describe internal and external sources of liquidity and briefly discuss any material unused sources of liquid assets. [S-K 303(b)(1)(i)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital resources disclosure — cash requirements, sources, purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss material cash requirements (including material commitments for capital expenditures) as of the latest fiscal period; anticipated sources of funds and general purpose of such requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe known material trends (favorable or unfavorable) in capital resources and any reasonably likely material changes in the mix and relative cost of equity, debt, and off-balance-sheet financing arrangements. [S-K 303(b)(1)(ii)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Address material contractual and off-balance-sheet obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Liquidity and capital resources discussion should address material cash requirements from known contractual obligations and commitments or contingent obligations from arrangements with unconsolidated entities that could materially affect financial condition or liquidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose commitments even when the arrangement results in no obligations on consolidated balance sheets. Examples include guarantees; retained or contingent interests in transferred assets; contractual arrangements supporting credit/liquidity/market risk for transferred assets; variable interests in unconsolidated entities; obligations related to derivative instruments indexed to and classified in registrant's own equity. [Instruction 4 and 8 to S-K 303(b)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt instruments, guarantees and covenant disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss debt instruments, guarantees and related covenants where disclosure is likely necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is likely necessary if the registrant is or is reasonably likely to be in breach of debt covenants or if covenants impact the ability to obtain additional debt or equity financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidity discussion — focus on drivers, not restatement of cash flow statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should not simply repeat items reported in the statement of cash flows; focus on primary drivers and other material factors necessary to understand cash flows and the indicative value of historical cash flows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe operating, investing and financing cash flows associated with discontinued operations separately from continuing operations if not apparent from cash flow statement, and discuss how liquidity is affected by absence of discontinued operations' cash flows. See Section 9830.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of operations — analyze causes, not merely numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The discussion should not consist merely of numeric dollar and percentage changes period-to-period; focus on analysis of factors that caused changes and any material offsetting changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe underlying reasons for material changes in quantitative and qualitative terms; consider discussing key variables and financial measures management uses (including non-financial or industry-specific metrics) to manage the business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures for results of operations [S-K 303(b)(2)]
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose: unusual/infrequent events or significant economic changes that materially affected income from continuing operations; significant components of revenues and expenses material to understanding results; known trends or uncertainties reasonably likely to materially affect net sales/revenues or income; events reasonably likely to change the relationship between costs and revenues; and when material changes in net sales/revenue occur, describe extent attributable to price vs volume vs new products/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed item in S-K 303(b)(2) must be addressed to the extent material to understanding results of operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment and subdivision discussion where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Where discussion of segment information or other subdivisions (geographic, product lines) is necessary to understand the business, focus on each reportable segment and on the registrant as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment analysis may be integrated with consolidated discussion to avoid repetition; avoid unnecessary length or obscuring salient information. Discuss all material components of results, including items not allocated to segments (e.g., corporate overhead, income taxes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss tax implications and reconciling items
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider discussing and analyzing tax implications related to material transactions, trends and other important items in MD&A, including nature and impact of significant tax rate reconciling items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, discuss tax rate reconciling items from changes in assumptions for unrecognized tax benefits or different final resolutions; when uncertain tax positions are a critical accounting estimate, address why assumptions changed or why resolution differed from assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain price vs volume mix and underlying factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Address underlying reasons for changes in price versus volume mix; do not stop after identifying price and volume components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss factors contributing to volume decline or price increases, and consider foreign currency fluctuations when discussing price vs volume changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When basis changes occur consider pro forma supplemental discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: When results are not prepared on a consistent basis (e.g., material acquisition, pushdown accounting, fresh-start accounting), consider whether MD&A should be supplemented by discussion based on pro forma information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider facts and circumstances, nature of pro forma adjustments, and meaningfulness of supplemental pro forma discussion. If pro forma is used, present in a format consistent with S-X Article 11 (or other appropriate formats) and limit pro forma presentations to most recent fiscal year and interim period prior to transaction, subject to S-X 11-02(c)(2)(i) limitations and examples in guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma presentation — explain derivation and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If pro forma results are discussed in MD&A, explain how the pro forma presentation was derived, why management believes it is useful, and any potential risks associated with using such a presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically complete pro forma financial information (reflecting adjustments) will be necessary to facilitate understanding; narrative disclosure of limited pro forma adjustments may suffice in some situations. Pro forma discussion should not be presented with greater prominence than historical financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify contributions of acquisitions and avoid vague statements
rubrics_metrics.description: MD&A should fully explain results of operations; do not merely state that increases are due to a significant acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify the contribution of the acquisition to total revenues to the extent possible, and address increases or decreases in the underlying revenues of the pre-existing business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key performance indicators and metrics — definition and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: When metrics (KPIs) are disclosed, they should generally be accompanied by a clear definition and how they are calculated; a statement why the metric provides useful information to investors; and a statement indicating how management uses the metric in managing or monitoring performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether there are estimates or assumptions underlying the metric that should be disclosed so the metric is not materially misleading. (Release No. 33-10751)

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in metric calculation or presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company changes how it calculates or presents a metric, it should consider disclosing, to the extent material: differences vs prior periods, reasons for changes, effects on amounts previously reported, and other methodology differences relevant to understanding performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on significance, consider recasting prior metrics to conform to current presentation and place current disclosure in appropriate context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of known trends, demands, commitments, events or uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: Management must assess whether a known trend/demand/commitment/event/uncertainty is likely to come to fruition, and if not reasonably likely no disclosure is required; if management cannot determine likelihood, evaluate consequences assuming it will occur and disclose unless management determines a material effect is not reasonably likely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose known trends, demands, commitments, events or uncertainties that are not remote or where management cannot assess likelihood and that would reasonably be likely to have a material effect on future results or financial condition if they came to fruition. A reasonable investor would consider omission to significantly alter the mix of information. Note: 'reasonably likely' is lower than 'more likely than not' but higher than 'remote'. (Release No. 33-6835; Release No. 33-10890)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim period MD&A requirements [S-K 303(c)]
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide MD&A for interim periods to enable assessment of material changes in financial condition and results of operations between periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim MD&A must include discussion of material changes in financial condition since the preceding fiscal year-end, changes in year-to-date results vs prior year-to-date, and quarter-to-quarter comparisons (with rules on which periods to compare and when to provide summary financial information). Registrants may presume the reader has access to the prior year's MD&A and should focus on material changes; seasonal or other items immaterial annually may be material in interim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for forward-looking information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any forward-looking information supplied is covered by the safe harbors in Rule 175 under the Securities Act and Rule 3b-6 under the Exchange Act for projections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe harbors protect forward-looking statements made or reaffirmed with a reasonable basis and in good faith against certain private legal actions alleging material misstatements or omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAB Topic 11M (SAB 74) — disclosure for recently issued accounting standards not yet adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: SAB Topic 11M provides guidance for registrants regarding recently issued accounting standards not yet adopted, highlighting types of disclosures to consider in MD&A and financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally unnecessary to provide duplicative disclosure in MD&A and financial statements nor to provide disclosure for standards that will not apply to a registrant. Registrants should exercise judgment consistent with the SAB in determining nature, extent, and location of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign private issuers — Item 5 of Form 20-F (OFR) parallels S-K 303
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 5 of Form 20-F calls for the same disclosure as S-K 303; the OFR requirements include Operating results (5.A), Liquidity and capital resources (5.B), Research and development/patents/licenses (5.C), Trend information (5.D), and Critical Accounting Estimates (5.E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion must focus on primary financial statements and, where applicable, reconcile home-country GAAP and U.S. GAAP differences necessary for understanding the financial statements as a whole. IFRS reporters must provide disclosure satisfying objectives of Item 5. Instruction references include interpretive releases cited for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical accounting estimates — definition and disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical accounting estimates are GAAP estimates that involve significant estimation uncertainty and have had or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on financial condition or results of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide qualitative and quantitative information necessary to understand estimation uncertainty and the impact of each critical estimate, including why each estimate is subject to uncertainty, how much each estimate/assumption has changed over a relevant period (if material and reasonably available), and sensitivity of reported amounts to methods, assumptions and estimates underlying the calculation. When assumptions are interdependent, disclose assumptions held constant in sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goodwill impairment — suggested disclosures for reporting units at risk
rubrics_metrics.description: For each reporting unit at risk of failing the quantitative impairment test, consider disclosing: percentage by which fair value exceeded carrying value at most recent test; amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit; description of methods and key assumptions used, how they were determined and how they changed; discussion of degree of uncertainty associated with assumptions; and description of potential events/changes that could negatively affect assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reporting unit may be at risk if fair value is not substantially in excess of carrying value; registrants need not provide these disclosures if they assert and disclose that material goodwill does not exist at reporting units at risk or that no reporting units are at risk — provide supporting rationale if not disclosing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share-based compensation in IPOs — valuation and disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: In IPO prospectuses, disclose methods used to determine fair value of the company's shares and the nature of material assumptions (e.g., income approach requires estimating future cash flows and discount rate); disclose specific factors making estimates complex/subjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates may not be necessary once shares begin trading; companies may cross-reference other prospectus disclosure. The staff may comment on unusual valuations and request analyses to confirm appropriate accounting; also consider MD&A requirements related to share-based compensation (known trends, expected impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Related party transaction disclosures in MD&A
rubrics_metrics.description: Where related party transactions are material, supplement S-K 404 disclosures with additional MD&A discussion necessary for understanding current and prospective financial position and operating results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure may include business purpose of arrangement; identification of related parties; how transaction prices were determined; description of fairness evaluation methods if fairness is claimed; any ongoing contractual or other commitments. Consider disclosing arrangements with parties outside formal related-party definitions if they enable negotiating terms not available to arms-length parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A for registration and proxy statements when financials are retroactively revised
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration and proxy statements that include annual financial statements retroactively revised to report discontinued operations, revised segment reporting, or application of a different accounting principle should include a revised MD&A based on revised financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss events/circumstances leading to discontinued operation, material terms of termination, impact on operating results and business; discuss contingent obligations, continuing relationships, impact on liquidity and capital resources, and reasonably likely effect on continuing business and financial health. For segment or accounting principle revisions, explain changes in resource allocation/assessment of performance and related trends based on revised disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional MD&A guidance references
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff retained various releases and sample letters as additional guidance sources for MD&A (concept releases, interpretive releases, staff summaries and sample letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References include Concept Release on MD&A (No. 33-6711), Releases No. 33-6835, 33-8056, 33-8350, staff summaries, SAB and interpretive/adopting releases such as No. 33-9144, No. 33-10751, No. 33-10890, and various sample letters (e.g., mortgage/foreclosure, SFAS 157/ASC 820). Registrants should be aware some components may have been superseded.
